script.opening_words: You're making $85,000 a year and somehow you're still broke. Meanwhile, your friend who makes $52,000 just booked a trip to Japan and has six months of expenses saved. The math isn't mathing and it's driving you insane. Here's what nobody tells you about building wealth. You're trying to play offense and defense at the same time, and you're losing at both. Like, you're clipping coupons while also working 60hour weeks. You're meal prepping chicken and rice while simultaneously paying
script.ending_words: of trying at everything and excelling at nothing. Your 20s are burning away whether you use them or not. Your income potential has an expiration date and every month you spend optimizing the wrong variable is a month you can't get back. So stop pretending you can do both. Pick your phase, commit fully, and actually build something instead of just staying busy. That's it. No, that's the whole game.
script.analysis: Full 21443 canonical characters read. An opinion framework: hook contrasting an $85K broke earner with a $52K saver, the bulking/cutting analogy, what bulking means (income growth, self-investment, job switching), the trap of staying in bulking, what cutting means, phase-by-age guidance, worked examples (rent, car, phone), a 12-month test, numerical comparisons of coupon savings vs raises, compounding of early earnings, transition psychology and an action plan by age/income. Arithmetic largely reproduces at stated assumptions (233%, $412K with monthly contributions, $435K/$93K at 8%, $375/hour). Weak points: job-switch premium was negative for much of 2025 (Atlanta Fed); "generational wealth" from a $650 payment (~$48K); age cut-offs and course/raise links are unevidenced; "$2,400 car payment" likely garbled. Few external factual claims. The stored ending is complete.

claim_audit.assessment: ATLWGT: Atlanta Fed Wage Growth Tracker historically shows a switcher premium, but stayers out-earned switchers Feb-Jul 2025 (first since 2018); the premium returned to ~0.8 pt by September 2025.
